application.source: classification mapping required by the facts audit brief

chemistry.note: Neither the release nor its paper or record states the cell chemistry.

units_released.note: Rule: one vehicle. Released unit identifiers require package-specific inspection.

cells_liion.source: the 108 columns of V_cell_bms, through fielddata.loaders.stanford_ev
cells_liion.note: The release's 108 cell-voltage channels, counted as released. The record does not name the vehicle, and it is not taken to be the Audi e-tron of the group's companion paper (doi:10.1109/OJPEL.2026.3691252, 4P108S, 432 cells): the paper says that car's pack was taken apart after January 2024, but this release shows one pack in use, with the same cell-voltage pattern and a rising odometer, from September 2021 to April 2025 (scripts/checks/stanford_ev_timeline.py). Maintainer, 2026-10-16: the match cannot be shown, so the data's count is used.

cells_leadacid.note: No lead-acid cell count applies or is exposed in this release.

cell_channels_measured.source: the 108 columns of V_cell_bms, through fielddata.loaders.stanford_ev

energy_mwh.note: Present usable energy computed from the data: coulomb counting over runs of at least 40 points of SOC with no gap over 300 s, ampere-hours per 100 percent SOC times mean pack voltage, median per unit, summed. The record does not name the vehicle.

energy_basis.source: energy_mwh is computed from the released data

span_unit_years.note: unit-years is first session start to last session end; CC BY-NC-ND: only these counts are recorded, no derived data files

obs_hours.note: Calendar spans are measurable, so observation-hours are not used.

fault_onset_timestamp.source: docs/descriptor/TABLE3_faults.md; released labels and metadata contain no explicit fault-onset timestamp field

sentinels_documented.source: https://doi.org/10.25740/yx490wc6642; public data record and released documentation state no sentinel convention
